title: Pathway memories can form through dynamics alone, without structural change

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Pathway memories can form through dynamics alone, without structural change

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In ODE models of biological pathways, memories (such as associative memory, in which a neutral stimulus becomes a conditioned stimulus) can be formed by patterns of stimulation through dynamical interactions alone, without changing the network's structure or parameters.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.1. Biological Networks May Possess Multiple Types of Memory

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Again, while feedback loop architecture is present, our results indicate that memories can be formed through dynamical interactions alone, without changing network structure/architecture.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “2. Results › 2.1. Biological Networks May Possess Multiple Types of Memory”. Scope: ODE models of gene regulatory and protein pathways (e.g. MAPK cascade models)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-08: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.90

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a clean computational intervention with an explicit invariant: structure and parameters remain fixed. Public models and methods make direct replication practical.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Hold every model equation and parameter fixed, apply only the specified time-varying stimuli, and test whether post-training responses satisfy associative-memory criteria. Any hidden parameter or structural update, or failure of the response, would refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Numerical state changes must be distinguished from parameter or structural changes.

Threshold choices affect classification.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.95
data adequacy: 0.86
discriminating power: 0.94
analysis feasibility: 0.84
data existence: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The methods fix the ODE system and apply stimuli by clamping a variable, then score persistence after release. Public code and the original models make that contrast re-runnable. If the stored response survives with the same equations, the claim about these pathway models is confirmed or refuted directly.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Rerun associative and other memory assays while logging whether rate parameters and the reaction graph stay fixed, and test whether the response remains altered after the clamp is released. Persistent change with an unchanged model file would confirm dynamical memory; memory that appears only after an edit to parameters or edges would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: A temporary clamp is an external drive, which a rival description can treat as a transient parameter change.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.85
operationalizability: 0.88
analysis feasibility: 0.62
discriminating power: 0.72
data adequacy: 0.8
